title: Uniform degree bound for homogeneous initial ideals
statement: Fix integers $r,D\geq1$. There is an integer $G(r,D)\geq1$ with the following property for every field $k$ [def-weil-field]. In $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], let $J$ be an ideal generated by homogeneous polynomials of total degree at most $D$; homogeneous means every monomial with nonzero coefficient has the same total exponent sum. Let $\prec$ be any monomial order: a total well-order on $\mathbf N^r$, with $0$ least, preserved by addition, and define $\operatorname{LM}_\prec(f)$ to be the greatest exponent occurring in a nonzero polynomial $f$. Then there is a finite family of nonzero homogeneous elements $g_1,\ldots,g_s\in J$ of degrees at most $G(r,D)$ such that the monomial ideal generated by $x^{\operatorname{LM}_\prec(f)}$ for all $0\ne f\in J$ is generated by $x^{\operatorname{LM}_\prec(g_j)}$, $1\leq j\leq s$. The integer $G(r,D)$ is independent of the field, its characteristic, the generators and the order. The zero ideal is included with an empty family, and the unit ideal with the element $1$.

source.place: Dube, The Structure of Polynomial Ideals and Groebner Bases, SIAM J. Comput. 19 (1990), pp.750--773, Theorem 8.2 and Corollary 8.3, printed p.773. Only existence of a degree bound is used; local PDF WANTED, primary article read online. No Stacks tag states this effective bound.

proof.text: For $J=0$ use the empty family; for $J=S$ use $1$. For the remaining ideals take any generating set of nonzero homogeneous polynomials of degree at most $D$, divide each by its leading coefficient, and call the resulting set $B_0$. This need not be finite. Scalar normalization does not change the generated ideal, homogeneity, degree or leading exponent. Put $h(i)=2^{i+1}D$, choose $L=L(r,h)$ from [lem-sfb-controlled-exponent-sequence-length], and set $G(r,D)=2^L D\geq1$. These choices involve only $r,D$.

source.place: Agent existence-only proof of the uniform-bound conclusion of Dube Theorem 8.2 (printed p.773), via controlled exponent sequences and Buchberger completion; not the sharper cone-decomposition proof of the numerical bound. Local PDF WANTED; primary article read online.

proof.text: Here is the homogeneous division used in the construction. Given a set $B$ of nonzero homogeneous polynomials and a homogeneous polynomial $p$ of degree $e$, apply [lem-sfb-monomial-order-polynomial-division] to get $p=\sum q_b b+v$, with finite support and the stated leading-exponent and remainder-support bounds. Write $d_b=\deg b$. Taking the degree-$e$ part coefficientwise gives $p=\sum (q_b)_{e-d_b}b+v_e$, interpreting a negative-degree part as zero. Indeed a monomial in $q_b$ contributes in degree $e$ precisely when its degree is $e-d_b$. Each retained product is a homogeneous component of $q_b b$, so all its exponents remain at most $\operatorname{LM}(p)$; the same is true of $v_e$, by the equality. Its support is a subset of that of $v$, hence avoids every leading exponent of $B$ coordinatewise. Thus the projected remainder is zero or homogeneous of degree $e$, is reduced in that support sense, and lies in $(B)$ whenever $p$ does. If $p=0$ use the zero representation.

proof.text: Inductively maintain $B_t\subset J$, monic and homogeneous, generating $J$, with every degree at most $2^tD$. If every pair in $B_t$ has the strict standard representation required by [lem-sfb-buchberger-standard-representation-criterion], stop. Otherwise choose a pair $b,c$ lacking one and put $\lambda=\operatorname{LM}(b)\vee\operatorname{LM}(c)$. Its polynomial $p=x^{\lambda-\operatorname{LM}(b)}b-x^{\lambda-\operatorname{LM}(c)}c$ is homogeneous of degree $e=|\lambda|\leq\deg b+\deg c\leq2^{t+1}D$. Both top terms are $x^\lambda$ and cancel, so $p=0$ or $\operatorname{LM}(p)\prec\lambda$. Step 2 gives $p=\sum q_u u+v$, with every nonzero product and the remainder having leading exponent strictly below $\lambda$. The remainder cannot be zero, since that would give the missing strict representation. Adjoin $v/\operatorname{LC}(v)$ to form $B_{t+1}$. The remainder belongs to $J$ by the division equality, has degree $e$, and its leading exponent dominates no leading exponent of $B_t$. All induction invariants follow.

proof.text: If $n$ additions occur, index their remainder leading exponents by $\alpha_i$ for $0\leq i<n$. Step 3 gives $|\alpha_i|\leq2^{i+1}D=h(i)$. For $i<j$ the $i$th remainder already belongs, after normalization, to $B_j$, while the $j$th remainder is reduced against $B_j$. Hence $\alpha_i\not\leq\alpha_j$ coordinatewise. By [lem-sfb-controlled-exponent-sequence-length], $n\leq L$. Consequently the construction must stop at some $t\leq L$: failure at each stage $0,\ldots,L$ would construct $L+1$ such exponents. This is finite recursion, requiring no fairness or enumeration of the possibly infinite family of pairs.

proof.text: At the stopping stage the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-buchberger-standard-representation-criterion] hold for $B_t$ and its generated ideal $J$. Every nonzero $f\in J$ therefore has $x^{\operatorname{LM}(f)}$ divisible by some $x^{\operatorname{LM}(b)}$, $b\in B_t$. The reverse ideal inclusion holds because $B_t\subset J$. Thus these leading monomials generate exactly the required initial monomial ideal.

source.place: Agent existence-only proof of the uniform-bound conclusion of Dube Theorem 8.2 (printed p.773), via controlled exponent sequences and Buchberger completion; not the sharper cone-decomposition proof of the numerical bound. Local PDF WANTED; primary article read online.

proof.text: Every $b\in B_t$ is nonzero homogeneous of degree at most $2^tD\leq G(r,D)$, so each coordinate of $\operatorname{LM}(b)$ lies in $\{0,\ldots,G(r,D)\}$. There are finitely many such tuples (at most $(G(r,D)+1)^r$). For each tuple actually occurring choose one member of $B_t$ with that leading exponent, giving a finite family $g_1,\ldots,g_s$. Its leading monomials are exactly those occurring for $B_t$, so step 5 gives the desired generation statement. Its elements lie in $J$, are homogeneous, and have the required degree bound. All choices and inequalities work over any field, without a characteristic assumption or a degree-compatible-order assumption.

lean.statement: theorem exists_uniform_homogeneous_groebner_degree_bound (r D : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hD : 1 ≤ D) : ∃ G : ℕ, 1 ≤ G ∧ ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] (J : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin r) k)) (m : MonomialOrder.{0, v} (Fin r)), (∃ B : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin r) k), Ideal.span B = J ∧ ∀ f ∈ B, f.IsHomogeneous f.totalDegree ∧ f.totalDegree ≤ D) → ∃ (s : ℕ) (g : Fin s → MvPolynomial (Fin r) k), (∀ i, g i ∈ J ∧ g i ≠ 0 ∧ (g i).IsHomogeneous (g i).totalDegree ∧ (g i).totalDegree ≤ G) ∧ Ideal.span ((fun f : MvPolynomial (Fin r) k ↦ MvPolynomial.monomial (m.degree f) (1 : k)) '' {f : MvPolynomial (Fin r) k | f ∈ J ∧ f ≠ 0}) = Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin s ↦ MvPolynomial.monomial (m.degree (g i)) (1 : k))) ∧ (J = ⊥ → s = 0) ∧ (J = ⊤ → s = 1 ∧ ∀ i : Fin s, g i = 1)
